references.summary: Annual cereal; product and cultivar affect harvest stage. Winter hardiness depends on growth habit and acclimation; reproductive growth is more vulnerable. Heat around reproduction and grain filling can reduce grain number and size. Rotating only between cereals may retain shared cereal pathogens and grass hosts. Earlier maturity can help escape terminal drought, but this is cultivar- and sowing-date-dependent.
